collection.description: This year a villager has been chosen to dance.

ask.text:
Once a generation, the village brings out two carved masks kept wrapped in the elders' hut: one of a very old face, one of a child's face. At the harvest dance, one person wears each, and the old stories say the masks "lend their years" for the length of a song, and sometimes forget to take them back.
This year (name) has been chosen to dance. The elders hold out both masks. (Name) can choose which to wear.
Which should (name) choose?

c1o1.text: When the song ends and (name) takes the mask off, the elders go quiet. The mask has kept its years where they were: in (name). (He/She) is ten years older, grey at the temples, with the old ones' slow way of standing. "It forgets sometimes," says the eldest. "It's very old." (Name) sits down with the elders that night, and finds the conversation better than expected.

c1o2.text: When the mask comes off, (name)'s face is younger, not older. The elders are puzzled, then delighted. "It lent you its years," says the eldest, "and you gave them back with interest." Nobody quite knows what that means, but (name) looks wonderful.

c1.text: The old mask is heavy, and smells of smoke and wood oil. Behind it, (name) feels (his/her) back bend and (his/her) steps slow, and (he/she) dances the old dance the way the old ones did...

c2o1.text: When the song ends and the mask comes off, (name) is breathless and flushed and five years younger. Not a child, but younger, with five years of aches and worries simply gone. "That one forgets as well," says the eldest, a little enviously. (Name) dances till dawn.

c2o2.text: The mask comes off, and (name) is (himself/herself), just very hot and very happy. The children make (him/her) do the running dance again, and again, until (he/she) begs for mercy. The masks are wrapped up and put away for another generation.

c2.text: The child's mask is light as a leaf. Behind it, (name) feels like running, and does, round and round the fire, laughing, while the drums go faster and faster...
